title: 📰 AI news · October 13
takeaway: Today's stories share one thread: AI agents now work with real systems, and you can see it on both sides. One attacker built 51 agents on Claude Code and reached hundreds of sites, while Meta and Epic Games build their work around models and agents. If you work with AI, protect your website, keys and passwords on the site itself, because a model's refusal only holds inside a single conversation.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder, models at the frontier level
items.text: By Meta's own numbers, Muse Wonder and Wonder Full match Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. Wonder costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. Wonder Full is for Muse Code subscribers, and both models remember user data over long periods.

items.title: Hacker ran 51 Claude Code agents and stole 628,000 records
items.text: The CyberXero group reached 429 WordPress admin panels and planted 32 web shells in 61 seconds in one run. It got around model refusals by opening a new session with a pre-written cover story. Data theft from four Ukrainian organizations is confirmed.

items.title: Spy implant found in Ledger wallets from a reseller
items.text: All confirmed cases trace back to the reseller CryptoBilis in Southeast Asia. Analyst Specter estimates losses above $86 million. Ledger and the reseller halted sales.

items.title: SonicWall SMA 1000 flaw rated 10 of 10 attacked 135 times after the patch
items.text: CVE-2026-102255 lets an attacker make the server reach internal addresses without a password. The patch came out on October 6, and attack attempts continue. Update the firmware.

items.title: 8.6 million karaoke customer records leaked
items.text: Malware infected the contractor Nippon Columbia and exposed customer and employee data of Daiichi Kosho. Which fields were affected is still unknown.

items.title: Norway fines Microsoft's ad firm Xandr $9.6 million
items.text: Xandr unlawfully shared sensitive data of Grindr users. The decision comes from the Norwegian data protection regulator.

items.title: Cyberattack switched off fridges in French supermarkets
items.text: Attackers remotely shut down cooling by targeting Danfoss controllers. The chains involved and the size of the losses are not yet known.

items.title: Ahold Delhaize takes some systems offline after a cyberattack
items.text: The retailer, which owns supermarket chains in Europe and the US, took part of its systems offline. The scale and recovery time have not been announced.

items.title: Epic Games moves to AI-first development
items.text: Bloomberg reports that Epic delayed its Disney project and asked developers to use AI more. Tim Sweeney called it a huge pivot toward faster work with AI.

items.title: Amazon in talks to buy Decart for $7 billion
items.text: The Wall Street Journal reports talks with the maker of real-time video models. No deal is signed yet; Anthropic walked away from a $6 billion purchase in September.

items.title: Falcon-ASR turns Arabic speech into text, including Emirati dialect
items.text: The 1.6-billion-parameter model from the TII institute has a 20.92% average word error rate on six Arabic tests. It also handles English, French, Spanish and Portuguese.

items.title: Apple holds its "Welcome Home" event today at 9:00 New York time
items.text: A smart home hub with a screen of about 6 inches, a new HomePod mini and an Apple TV 4K are expected. Apple has not said what it will actually show.
